crossRefs.note: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
“My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters…
But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree. Then he requested…
Therefore now, Yahweh, take, I beg you, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.”
When the sun arose, God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat on Jonah’s head, so that he fainted, and…
Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
Look away from him, that he may rest, until he accomplishes, as a hireling, his day.
Remove your scourge away from me. I am overcome by the blow of your hand.
Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away and exist no more.”
Surely men of low degree are just a breath, and men of high degree are a lie. In the balances they will go up. They are…
Therefore he consumed their days in vanity, and their years in terror.
Man is like a breath. His days are like a shadow that passes away.
For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can…

translations.web: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
translations.bsb: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
translations.kjv: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.
translations.asv: I loathe my life; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.
